answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks that require scarce, independently verified resources, such as a signed delivery receipt from a wharf. A prism-like audit randomly checks the work against physical evidence, while repeated claims from linked wallets share one reputation stake. A sybil operator must therefore lock real capital and acquire scarce resources for every identity; failed audits slash the stake, making fabricated accounts costly rather than free. Even pigment on a parcel can serve as a detail an auditor checks, not proof by itself.
